matches.rationale: The ground-truth describes unrealistically large and suspiciously consistent success-rate improvements (nearly 5% on R2R-CE, over 13% on REVERIE-CE) to cast doubt on data integrity. No finding addresses this issue; findings 4 and 5 point out text-table numerical inconsistencies involving different claimed percentages, which is a separate factual-error issue.

Finding 1 identifies a logical flaw in the Frustum Culling removal condition that would cause occluded/stale features to be retained. This concretely embodies the ground-truth's complaint that the updating mechanism is inconsistent and that it is unclear how stale patches are discarded to maintain multi-view consistency.

The ground-truth concerns an exaggerated novelty claim in the Introduction about previous methods focusing only on mask accuracy. No finding mentions this rhetorical distortion or the comparison with prior 3D segmentation methods.

Finding 6 demonstrates that the pre-exploration protocol provides privileged environment information and that Table 3 compares this privileged result against a non-privileged baseline, inflating apparent gains. This matches the ground-truth's design flaw of potential memorization/environment leakage and unfairly large performance claims.
The ground-truth highlights missing ethics/safety approvals for the real-world robot experiments. None of the findings address ethical omissions, consent, or safety protocols.
The ground-truth describes overconfident language in the abstract ('sets new state-of-the-art performance') that inflates significance. No finding reports rhetorical overstatement in the abstract.
The ground-truth points to a misleading Related Work narrative that omits concurrent work to exaggerate novelty. No finding addresses the coverage or fairness of the literature review.

The ground-truth identifies an overclaim in the Conclusion inconsistent with modest experimental results and acknowledged limitations. No finding involves cross-section inconsistencies between the conclusion and the experiments.

Finding 3 reveals that the text claims an ablation on degrading 3D instance/zone embeddings (feature dropout, spatial jitter) but Table 7 shows only SLAM and depth noise, making the robustness claim unsupported. This directly corresponds to the ground-truth’s criticism that representation-quality degradation was not actually tested.
The ground-truth concerns missing ethical-use and data-privacy statements in the Appendix. No finding discusses ethical omission in the dataset/appendix description.

The ground-truth states that the claim of balancing real-time adaptability and long-term memory lacks supporting quantitative metrics (e.g., latency, memory saturation). No finding addresses missing memory/adaptability analysis.

The ground-truth describes absolute, unqualified language in the Introduction bullet points ('achieves state-of-the-art performance') that may mislead. No finding reports rhetorical manipulation or overclaiming in the Introduction.
